name: All Sea Charters
summary: Family-owned whale watching cruises from Augusta, Busselton and Dunsborough on Western Australia's south west coast, run on Whale Song, a 17 metre catamaran built for whale watching. Augusta tours run in the early part of the whale season and Busselton and Dunsborough tours in the later part. The operator also hires Whale Song for private charters and runs a summer snorkelling trip to Carnac Island from Fremantle.
standouts: Family owned and operated, running charters in the south west since 2001
Whale Song is a 17 metre aluminium catamaran built for whale watching, with tours limited to 47 guests
Wheelchair accessible on the Busselton tour, with a boarding ramp and a viewing area on the main deck

trips.title: Augusta Whale Watching
trips.summary: A whale watching cruise of about two hours from Augusta Boat Harbour on Whale Song, a 17 metre catamaran built for whale watching. The crew look for Southern Right and Humpback whales migrating past Flinders Bay and talk guests through what they see. Augusta runs in the early part of the season, from May to late August.
highlights: Whale Song has two outside viewing decks, a climate-controlled cabin and onboard toilets
Southern Right and Humpback whales on their migration
trips.season: May to late August, daily departures
includes: Commentary from the crew on whale behaviour and local marine life
bring: Layered clothing and a windbreaker or waterproof jacket
Binoculars and a camera with a zoom lens
Anti-nausea medication if you are prone to seasickness (bracelets are available on board)
trips.requirements: Suitable for the whole family. No minimum age stated; infants 0 to 2 are free.

trips.title: Busselton Whale Watching
trips.summary: A whale watching cruise of about two and a half to three hours from Port Geographe Marina into Geographe Bay on Whale Song. Humpback and Southern Right whales are the main species, and Blue whales can also be seen. Whale Song has a boarding ramp and a wheelchair viewing area on this tour, and it runs from mid August to November.
highlights: Wheelchair accessible, with a boarding ramp and a dedicated viewing area on the main deck
Humpback and Southern Right whales, and sometimes Blue whales

trips.title: Boat Charters
trips.summary: Private hire of Whale Song from Busselton, Dunsborough and Bunbury for corporate events, family gatherings and celebrations. The boat carries up to 47 passengers in unprotected waters and up to 75 in protected waters, with a full kitchen, a bar area, a BBQ and a sound system. Guests can use the operator's catering partners or bring their own food and drinks.

trips.title: 4 Hour Adventure Tour
trips.summary: A four hour boat trip from Fremantle to Carnac Island, where Australian sea lions and bottlenose dolphins live, with swimming and snorkelling around the island. It runs in summer and leaves at 8:30am from Sardine Jetty.
highlights: Carnac Island, home to Australian sea lions, bottlenose dolphins and seabirds
Swimming and snorkelling in the waters around the island

checkNotes: The site answered normally throughout; no captcha or bot check was met. Whale watching, charters and the snorkel trip are the operator's own; the Rezdy account (whalewatchingcharters) is the operator's own and no rezdy.com or fareharbor.com page was opened. Each whale tour page embeds its own Rezdy product in a frame, and /book-now/ embeds the whole Rezdy tour catalog (catalog 155360), which was not opened, so any product that exists only in Rezdy is not captured. Phone is shown on the site as 0417 794 008. The email address is displayed through the site's email protection and was decoded from it; the footer gives only 'Busselton, Western Australia' as an address. Town is set to Busselton as the base; tours also leave from Augusta and Dunsborough. Left out as not the operator's own sea trips: (1) Swim with Dolphins and Dolphin Eco Cruise in Koombana Bay, Bunbury, which the swim-with-dolphins page says are offered by the Dolphin Discovery Centre and sold through a FareHarbor affiliate link (https://fareharbor.com/embeds/book/dolphindiscoverycentre/?ref=asn&asn=allseacharters-affiliate-aud&asn-ref=asn&full-items=yes), recorded here and not opened; its photos look like that business's and were left out of the media file. (2) Recreational Skippers Ticket (RST) training and assessing, $325 including government fees and boat hire, with assessing at Port Geographe Marina; a licence course rather than a sea trip, a person may want to add it as a course. (3) The old Perth eco tours page (last changed 2020) lists Carnac Island, Rottnest Island and Swan River cruises, private charters and corporate events on Tradewinds III and points to a sister site (perthswancruise.com.au) which was not read. (4) The whale-watching-margaret-river page repeats the three whale tours and adds nothing separate. (5) Educational tours for schools and groups are mentioned on the about and crew pages with no details. Gift vouchers are sold through Rezdy (catalog 583643; Adult product 317582, Child 659110, Family 659107) and are listed under offers. Prices are Australian dollars (the site shows only '$'). Home page says 'Tours starting from $65', which matches no current price (lowest child fare is $55, lowest adult fare is $95). The south-west-whale-watching-tours page still carries 2025 season wording and older vessel details (a second boat called Santosha, 52 ft, up to 23 passengers) that the current boats page does not mention. Booking policy (booking-policies page): for whale tours, full refund or reschedule more than 7 days out, a cancellation charge between 7 days and 48 hours, nothing within 48 hours, and the operator may change departure place or time slightly. Sighting guarantees ('see whales or go again for free'), a perfect safety record and Tripadvisor ranking claims appear throughout and are not repeated as fact; the Dolphin Discovery Centre page also states sighting and in-water success rates. Today's date is mid October 2026: Augusta (May to August) is out of season, and Busselton and Dunsborough are in season.
